svg.title: Remote worker lifecycle (v1.3, after Curator CIP-0009 revision 2): stop, leave and purge on the donor; suspend, retire and revoke on our side; the identity stays pinned unless revoked

g.text: Remote worker lifecycle (v1.3, after Curator CIP-0009 revision 2): stop, leave and purge on the donor; suspend, retire and revoke on our side; the identity stays pinned unless revoked
States: enrolled -> active <-> stopped (donor) | suspended (project) -> retired -> revoked -> purged.
Stop and revocation marks are persisted BEFORE any process is touched, so a service restart cannot race them.
Removing an SSH key never substitutes for closing established sessions and killing jobs.
persist "stopped"; end the harness identity's processes; keep the bridge service and the keys; audit line
donor: leave (retire the workplace, keep the identity)
retire request over the channel (if reachable)
close the channel; keep K_sig, K_enc, K_ssh and the configuration
left; "init --rejoin" with a new invitation returns this identity to a new workplace
revoke channel authorization; close open sessions
journaled stop of the workplace executions; confirm no process of the generation remains (F-19);
remove the authorized key; delete the home, keep only the service-generated metadata export (F-1);
next frame or envelope from this worker refused (retired); mailbox kept durable
the donor's connection drops; its bridge reports "retired by project" and pauses
revoke (only on compromise or departure): root-signed revocation of K_sig, K_enc, K_ssh
revocation record: every frame and envelope from these keys refuses from now on;
a return needs a new key through a new enrolment (rotation is a root-authorized record)
report purge; ask revocation outcome (if reachable)
record "channel unreachable; the project side must revoke separately"
delete keys, locked config, managed home; audit kept for the donor
remove donor accounts, homes, egress and sandbox
removed; nothing of the project remains on this machine; revocation outcome printed
